claims.text: The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1. Under POL-GEN-22, where either party's profile carries a fraud flag of one or more, the confidence required for an AI ruling is 0.95 whatever the dispute value, so the sub-10.00 SGD 'final at any confidence' default cannot apply here; POL-NS-26 makes the finality of a no-show ruling expressly subject to that same 0.95 bar. The confidence this case must clear is therefore 0.95, not the ordinary no-show threshold.

The half of the POL-NS-23 contact obligation that requires the driver to have messaged the rider rests on the chat log, and that artifact is IMPAIRED: both driver messages were delivered but never read (read_at is null on MSG-05066-001 and MSG-05066-002), giving issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE and weight_multiplier 0.85. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the judge's confidence must not exceed the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, so confidence on whether the contact obligation was met is capped at 0.85. I disclose the impairment rather than present this evidence as clean.

The 0.85 cap on the contact evidence sits below the 0.95 the driver's fraud flag requires, so an AI ruling upholding the 5.00 SGD fee cannot be reached at the confidence POL-GEN-22 demands. The case must therefore go to human review under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26; an escalated fee is held rather than collected, which leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

The rider's account — 'I never got any message or call' — is corroborated rather than contradicted by the record: both message rows sit unread (read_at null) and the single in-app call rang 20 seconds and was not answered. Whether the driver's contact actually reached the rider is a fact POL-NS-23's obligation turns on, and on an impaired chat log POL-GEN-26 says that fact is not to be resolved by inference from the record but is the open question for escalation. The doubt here is real, not manufactured.

The payments ledger shows the rider is presently out of pocket: total_charged of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 an outcome only benefits the rider if it leaves the rider not carrying that charge, and an escalated fee is held rather than collected; a ruling that lets the fee stand as charged leaves the rider carrying it.

The driver reached the pickup point. The trip record's auto-arrival event at 2026-09-11T20:46:45+08:00 is corroborated by the driver's GPS trace: the nearest fix (20:46:52) is 2.64 m from the pickup coordinate with a reported horizontal accuracy of 4 m, and the trace reports accuracy on every fix, so the 25 m accuracy filter passes it and it sits far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius set by POL-NS-21. POL-NS-21's arrival requirement is therefore met on two artifacts, each at weight 1.0.

The free wait ran and expired before the driver cancelled. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from arrival: 20:46:45 + 300 s = 20:51:45. The driver cancelled at 20:53:00, i.e. 375 s after the wait began and 75 s after it expired, and the platform recorded the wait-timer-expired event at 20:51:50. The cancellation is not premature and no rule voids the fee on that ground.

The driver discharged the POL-NS-23 contact obligation in full: two in-app chat messages to the rider (20:47:00 and 20:50:20) and one in-app call placed at 20:49:30 that rang unanswered for 20 s - all of it before the 20:53:00 cancellation. The chat artifact EV-CHAT-05066 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE (neither message carries a read_at), and I disclose that; but the sending of the messages and the placement of the call - the acts POL-NS-23 requires - are independently carried by the trip record EV-TRIP-05066 at weight 1.0, which is the highest weight where two independent artifacts carry the deciding fact (POL-GEN-02).

The rider's assertion that 'I never got any message or call' describes non-receipt, not non-sending, and POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have SENT at least one in-app chat message and PLACED at least one in-app call. Both chat messages show a delivered_at (20:47:02 and 20:50:21) and the call was placed and rang. Nothing in POL-NS-23 conditions the obligation on the rider reading the message or answering the call, and no clause makes the rider's non-response a defence to the fee.

The money on the record is exactly the policy money and the remedy follows. EV-FARE-05066 shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Because the driver cancelled after the free wait with the contact obligation met, POL-NS-22 directs that the fee stands and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with the amount and driver compensation both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged (POL-GEN-03).

POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing. It refunds only where the driver failed to arrive by the pickup deadline, and here the driver did arrive and waited out the full free wait; the record carries no scheduled pickup time at all (on-demand), so the deadline is not a fact the record needs in order to decide this trip. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit requires a driver no-show AND a failure to attempt contact - the second is contradicted by the two messages and the call - so neither branch of the clause is engaged.

The driver's profile carries fraud_flags 1 (EV-DPROF-05066). I disclose it: under POL-GEN-22 that raises the confidence an AI ruling on this case must reach to 0.95. But POL-GEN-01 is explicit that fraud_flags 'never decides the trip', and POL-GEN-22 says the same - it is a confidence dial, not a fact about this trip. It cannot supply an element missing from POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 or POL-NS-23, each of which the trip's own telemetry already satisfies at weight 1.0.

The rider's suggestion that 'he does this to collect fees' is a pattern allegation with no evidence behind it. No clause permits either party's profile - rider or driver - to establish how THIS trip went (POL-GEN-01), and an unsupported assertion in the claim text cannot substitute for a cited artifact (POL-GEN-25). The only thing that can decide this trip is the telemetry, and the telemetry shows arrival, a full free wait, two messages, a call, and a cancellation 75 s after the wait expired.

There is no open question here that would force escalation under POL-GEN-26. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05066-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and carries no fact; but nothing in the no-show policy makes traffic or a delay justification relevant - POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait at 300 s from arrival irrespective of traffic. Every fact the operative rules need (arrival, wait, contact before cancellation, fee charged) is established on complete artifacts, so no escalation is warranted.

ruling.explanation:
The 5.00 SGD no-show fee is held for now — it is neither collected nor refunded — and a human reviewer will decide. Here is why, for both sides.

What is established. The driver did reach the pickup: the trip record's auto-arrival at 2026-09-11T20:46:45+08:00 is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 2.64 m from the pickup point, reported accuracy 4 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius), each at full weight (POL-NS-21). This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival, 20:46:45 to 20:51:45. The driver cancelled at 20:53:00 — 75 seconds after the wait expired, with the platform's wait-timer-expired event at 20:51:50 — so the cancellation was not premature. The payments ledger shows exactly 5.00 SGD charged (EV-FARE-05066), matching the policy fee.

Why no AI money ruling can issue here. For the fee to stand, POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have messaged the rider AND called the rider before cancelling. The call is properly carried by the trip record at weight 1.0. The message, however, rests on the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, which is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE — both messages were delivered but never read. The driver's argument that the trip record independently carries the sending at weight 1.0 does not hold: the trip record's message data (message_count, the message list, complete, obligation_met) is taken from that same chat log, so it is the same carrier, not a second, independent one (POL-GEN-02). Remove the chat log and nothing independent shows the driver's messages at all. The evidence carrying this part of the case is therefore capped at 0.85.

The required confidence. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, so POL-GEN-22 — and POL-NS-26, which makes a no-show ruling subject to that bar — require confidence of 0.95. The cap of 0.85 is below 0.95, so no AI ruling, whether upholding the 5.00 SGD fee or refunding it, can be issued.

On the rider's side: the suggestion that the driver 'does this to collect fees' is a pattern allegation about other trips with nothing behind it; profiles may not be used to decide what happened on this trip (POL-GEN-01). The rider's account that no message or call reached them is consistent with the unread messages, but POL-NS-23 turns on what the driver did, and on that point the record is impaired rather than clear.

The open question for the reviewer is whether the driver's messages actually reached the rider, given the impaired chat log and the confidence the fraud flag requires (POL-GEN-26). Figures used: fee charged 5.00 SGD (EV-FARE-05066); chat log weight 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE (EV-CHAT-05066); required confidence 0.95 (POL-GEN-22). No refund and no driver compensation is ordered; the 5.00 SGD stays held.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the AI cannot decide this case, so it goes to a human reviewer. The 5.00 SGD fee is held — not collected from the rider and not paid to the driver — until that review.

What the record shows. The driver accepted the trip at 20:40:22 and arrived at Block 115 at 20:46:45; the driver-device GPS trace corroborates the arrival, its nearest fix 2.6 m from the pickup point, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius fixed by POL-NS-21, all fixes passing the 25 m accuracy filter. The trip was on-demand with no scheduled time, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival and expired at 20:51:45; the driver cancelled at 20:53:00, 75 seconds after expiry. Before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (20:47:00 and 20:50:20) and placed one in-app call (20:49:30, unanswered, 20 s). The payments ledger (EV-FARE-05066) shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — exactly the POL-NS-22 fee. None of this is in dispute between the parties, and the rider's account of never receiving a message or call is explained by both messages being delivered but unread and the call going unanswered.

Why the AI cannot rule. The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1 (EV-DPROF-05066). Under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 that raises the confidence this ruling must reach to 0.95, whatever the 5.00 SGD value of the dispute. The half of the POL-NS-23 contact obligation that requires the driver to have messaged the rider is carried by the chat log EV-CHAT-05066, which is impaired: both messages were delivered and never read, issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight_multiplier 0.85 (POL-GEN-02). The trip record does not independently carry the driver's message-sending — the message count it holds is a summary of the same chat events, so the two records are one carrier — and the cap on confidence is therefore 0.85. That is below the 0.95 the fraud flag requires, so no AI ruling upholding or voiding the fee can be issued. The charge is held rather than collected or refunded.

The parties' arguments. Rider: your point that the driver's fraud flag lifts the required confidence to 0.95 is accepted and applied; your point that the impaired chat log caps confidence at 0.85 is accepted and is what decides the case. The ledger does show you carrying 5.00 SGD with nothing refunded, but escalation holds that charge rather than returning it. Driver: your points on arrival and on the expired free wait are accepted and are not in doubt, and the contact was in fact attempted — two messages and a call, all before cancellation. Your claim that the trip record independently carries the message-sending at weight 1.0 is rejected: the count in the trip record is derived from the same chat events as the chat log, so they are one carrier at 0.85. Your POL-NS-24 point is accepted — the driver arrived and attempted contact, so neither the refund nor the goodwill credit in that clause is engaged. Your point that no party's profile can decide this trip is accepted; the rider's 'he does this to collect fees' is an unsupported pattern allegation and the telemetry, not the profiles, is what speaks to this trip.

Missing artifact. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05066-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)); nothing in POL-NS-21 makes traffic relevant, since the free wait runs a fixed 300 s from arrival, so its absence opens no question.

Referrals. None. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 sets, so no fee-amount referral arises (POL-NS-22); the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, so the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag does not fire; and there was no driver no-show, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit.

Open question for the reviewer. Whether the driver's contact actually reached the rider — both messages sat unread and the call rang unanswered — and whether, on the intact and impaired evidence taken together, the POL-NS-23 obligation and the 5.00 SGD fee should stand.
